name: Osaka
summary: Japan's merchant city on Osaka Bay: loud, friendly and food-obsessed, with neon over the Dotonbori canal, shotengai shopping arcades, manzai comedy, standing bars and a castle park, tied together by the Osaka Metro and a web of private railways.

curated-2026-10.title: Osaka places and neighborhoods written for Prospero Dungeon
curated-2026-10.note: Well-known public places, institutions and employers from general knowledge. Businesses open and close and rents move: treat this as a snapshot for fiction. Rents are rounded estimates of typical monthly asking ranges in yen, not listings. Coordinates are approximate neighborhood centers. Names use common Hepburn spellings without macrons.

curated-climate-2026-10.title: Approximate monthly climate for Osaka (Osaka Regional Meteorological Observatory)
curated-climate-2026-10.note: Rounded values in line with Japan Meteorological Agency 1991-2020 normals, converted to Fahrenheit; rain days count days with 1 mm or more. Refresh with scripts/world when network access to the JMA is available.

neighborhoods.name: Umeda
neighborhoods.summary: Kita's hub around Osaka and Umeda stations: department stores, underground malls, office towers, Grand Front Osaka and a maze of izakaya and karaoke on Higashi-dori.

neighborhoods.name: Nakazakicho and Chayamachi
neighborhoods.summary: Old wooden row houses that survived the war, turned into cafes, vintage shops and galleries a few minutes' walk from Umeda, beside the theaters of Chayamachi.

neighborhoods.name: Tenma and Tenjinbashisuji
neighborhoods.summary: Tenjinbashisuji, the longest shopping street in Japan, runs past Osaka Tenmangu shrine and a warren of cheap, packed izakaya around JR Tenma station.

neighborhoods.name: Fukushima
neighborhoods.summary: One stop west of Osaka station, a grid of small streets known across the city for izakaya, yakitori and oden, with the central wholesale market at Noda.

neighborhoods.name: Nakanoshima
neighborhoods.summary: The island between the Dojima and Tosabori rivers: City Hall, the red-brick Central Public Hall, art museums, Festival Hall and a rose garden at the eastern tip.

neighborhoods.name: Kitahama
neighborhoods.summary: The old financial quarter south of the Tosabori river, with the Osaka Exchange, Meiji and Taisho-era buildings and riverside terraces.

neighborhoods.name: Honmachi and Semba
neighborhoods.summary: The weekday business district along Midosuji boulevard: trading houses, textile wholesalers, pharmaceutical head offices in Doshomachi and the green strip of Utsubo Park.

neighborhoods.name: Shinsaibashi and Amerikamura
neighborhoods.summary: The covered Shinsaibashi-suji arcade and department stores on one side of Midosuji; on the other, Amerikamura's thrift shops, street fashion and clubs, running into Horie's boutiques.

neighborhoods.name: Dotonbori
neighborhoods.summary: The canal-side strip of giant food signs, the Glico running man, takoyaki stands and theaters, packed until late every night; the stone alley of Hozenji sits just behind it.

neighborhoods.name: Namba
neighborhoods.summary: Minami's rail hub: Nankai and Kintetsu terminals, Namba Parks, Takashimaya, the Sennichimae arcades and Namba Grand Kagetsu, the home of Yoshimoto comedy.

neighborhoods.name: Nipponbashi and Den Den Town
neighborhoods.summary: Kuromon Market's covered fish and produce stalls, the National Bunraku Theatre, and Den Den Town's electronics, anime, retro game and maid cafe strip along Sakaisuji.

neighborhoods.name: Shinsekai
neighborhoods.summary: A retro entertainment district built in 1912 under Tsutenkaku tower, all kushikatsu counters, shogi parlors and old-fashioned signs, between Tennoji Park and Spa World.

neighborhoods.name: Tennoji and Abeno
neighborhoods.summary: A southern hub around Tennoji station and Abeno Harukas, Japan's second-tallest building, with Shitennoji temple, Tennoji Park and the zoo.

neighborhoods.name: Tsuruhashi and Ikuno Koreatown
neighborhoods.summary: Where the smell of yakiniku greets you on the platform: a covered market of kimchi, hanbok and fish stalls, and the Koreatown shopping street, home to one of Japan's oldest Zainichi Korean communities.

neighborhoods.name: Osaka Castle and Morinomiya
neighborhoods.summary: The castle's moats, stone walls and huge park, with Osaka-jo Hall, the history museum and residential Morinomiya to the south-east.

neighborhoods.name: Kyobashi
neighborhoods.summary: A busy junction of the Loop Line and Keihan railway, famous for cheap standing bars that open in the morning, with the cherry trees of Sakuranomiya along the river.

neighborhoods.name: Juso
neighborhoods.summary: A gritty, friendly Hankyu junction just across the Yodo river from Umeda, with shopping arcades, late bars, a famous negiyaki shop and the fireworks on the riverbank.

neighborhoods.name: Bentencho and the Bay Area
neighborhoods.summary: The waterfront west of the center: Kaiyukan aquarium and the Tempozan wheel, Universal Studios Japan across the river at Sakurajima, Kyocera Dome, the port, and the Okinawan eateries of Taisho.

neighborhoods.name: Sumiyoshi
neighborhoods.summary: A calm southern district around Sumiyoshi Taisha, one of Japan's oldest shrines, with Nagai Park's stadiums and the Osaka Metropolitan University campus nearby.

neighborhoods.name: Nishinari and Kamagasaki
neighborhoods.summary: Osaka's poorest and oldest working district, where Kamagasaki's day labourers, now mostly elderly, live in small lodging-house rooms beside cheap diners, budget hostels and a strong network of community support groups.

neighborhoods.name: Suita
neighborhoods.summary: A northern suburb and university town: Expo '70 Commemorative Park and the Tower of the Sun, Osaka University's main campus, Kansai University and Gamba Osaka's stadium.

neighborhoods.name: Toyonaka and Minoh
neighborhoods.summary: Leafy commuter towns on the Hankyu lines below the hills, with Hattori Ryokuchi park, the Itami airport runway and the Minoo waterfall walk.

neighborhoods.name: Sakai
neighborhoods.summary: Osaka's southern neighbour, a medieval free port turned industrial city, known for keyhole-shaped imperial tombs, kitchen knives, Sen no Rikyu's tea and Sharp's bayside head office.

transit.name: Osaka Metro Midosuji Line
transit.summary: The red north-south trunk line under Midosuji boulevard, from Esaka (through to Senri-Chuo and Minoh) via Umeda, Namba and Tennoji to Nakamozu in Sakai; standing room only at rush hour.

transit.name: Osaka Metro Tanimachi Line
transit.summary: The purple line from Dainichi through Higashi-Umeda, Tenmabashi, Tanimachi 4-chome and Tennoji to Yaominami.

transit.name: Osaka Metro Yotsubashi Line
transit.summary: The blue line from Nishi-Umeda down the west side via Higobashi and Yotsubashi to Namba and Suminoekoen.

transit.name: Osaka Metro Chuo Line
transit.summary: The green east-west line from Nagata through Morinomiya, Tanimachi 4-chome and Honmachi to Osakako and Yumeshima.

transit.name: Osaka Metro Sennichimae Line
transit.summary: The pink line from Nodahanshin through Namba, Nipponbashi and Tsuruhashi to Minami-Tatsumi.

transit.name: Osaka Metro Sakaisuji Line
transit.summary: The brown line from Tenjinbashisuji 6-chome through Kitahama and Nipponbashi to Dobutsuen-mae and Tengachaya, running through to Hankyu trains for Kyoto.

transit.name: Osaka Metro Nagahori Tsurumi-ryokuchi Line
transit.summary: The light green line from Taisho through Shinsaibashi, Morinomiya and Kyobashi to Kadoma-minami.

transit.name: Osaka Metro Imazatosuji Line
transit.summary: The orange line through the eastern wards from Itakano to Imazato, linking with the Sennichimae Line.

transit.name: New Tram (Nanko Port Town Line)
transit.summary: Driverless rubber-tyred trains on an elevated guideway from Cosmosquare through the Nanko port district to Suminoekoen.

transit.name: JR Osaka Loop Line
transit.summary: The orange loop around the center through Osaka, Kyobashi, Tsuruhashi, Tennoji, Shin-Imamiya, Bentencho and Fukushima; trains run both ways.

transit.name: JR Yumesaki Line
transit.summary: The short branch from Nishikujo to Universal City and Sakurajima, often run with character-wrapped trains.

transit.name: Hankyu Railway
transit.summary: Maroon trains from Osaka-umeda to Kyoto, Kobe and Takarazuka, with branches to Minoo and Senri; every line crosses the river at Juso.

transit.name: Hanshin Electric Railway
transit.summary: The coastal line from Osaka-umeda to Kobe by way of Koshien Stadium, and the Namba Line to Nara through Kintetsu.

transit.name: Keihan Electric Railway
transit.summary: From Nakanoshima and Yodoyabashi along the Yodo river through Kyobashi, Kadoma and Hirakata to Kyoto.

transit.name: Nankai Electric Railway
transit.summary: From Namba south through Shin-Imamiya, Sumiyoshi Taisha and Sakai, and out to Kansai Airport and Wakayama.

transit.name: Kintetsu Railway
transit.summary: Japan's largest private railway, from Osaka-Namba, Osaka-Uehommachi and Osaka-Abenobashi to Nara, Ise and Nagoya, through Tsuruhashi.

transit.name: Osaka Monorail
transit.summary: An elevated monorail in an arc across the northern suburbs, from Osaka Airport through Senri-Chuo and Banpaku-kinen-koen (Expo park).

transit.name: Hankai Tramway
transit.summary: Osaka's last streetcars, rattling from Tennoji-ekimae and Ebisucho through Sumiyoshi to Sakai.

transit.name: Osaka trains, changing lines
transit.summary: Metro, JR and private railways meet at Umeda, Namba, Tennoji, Kyobashi and Tsuruhashi; most trips across town change trains once or twice on one ICOCA card.

transit.name: City and private buses
transit.summary: Osaka City Bus routes in the city, and Hankyu, Keihan, Kintetsu and Nankai buses in the suburbs; boarded at the middle door, paid at the front.

transit.name: Bike share and mamachari
transit.summary: Docked share bikes around the center, and everyone's own city bicycle with a basket and a child seat, parked in vast station lots.

places.name: Umeda Sky Building Floating Garden Observatory
places.summary: Open-air rooftop deck joining two towers forty floors up, with night views over the Yodo river.

places.name: Takimi Koji
places.summary: A recreated Showa-era alley of okonomiyaki, kushikatsu and izakaya counters in the basement of the Umeda Sky Building.

places.name: HEP FIVE Ferris Wheel
places.summary: Red Ferris wheel growing out of the roof of a youth fashion mall, fifteen minutes around above Umeda.

places.name: Grand Front Osaka
places.summary: Shops, restaurants and offices north of Osaka station, beside the Umekita lawns.

places.name: Umekita Park
places.summary: The large new park on the old freight yard north of Osaka station, with lawns, water play and events in front of the towers.

places.name: Hankyu Umeda Main Store food hall
places.summary: The busiest depachika in the city: bento, sweets, pickles and gift boxes, with the counters marked down near closing time.

places.name: Hanshin Umeda Main Store food hall
places.summary: The everyday department store basement, known for its long-running ikayaki squid-pancake stand.

places.name: Shin-Umeda Shokudogai
places.summary: A cramped two-level warren of cheap eateries and standing bars under the JR tracks, open since 1950.

places.name: Higashi-dori shopping street
places.summary: Umeda's nightlife arcade of izakaya chains, karaoke boxes, game centers and bars, loud until the last trains.

places.name: Salon de AManTo
places.summary: A ramshackle cafe and arts space in a century-old wooden house that helped start Nakazakicho's revival.

places.name: Nakazakicho row-house cafes
places.summary: Tiny cafes and sweet shops tucked into converted nagaya along the narrow lanes, each seating a handful.

places.name: Nakazakicho vintage and zakka shops
places.summary: Secondhand clothes, handmade goods and small galleries in old houses.

places.name: Umeda Arts Theater
places.summary: Large theater in Chayamachi for musicals, plays and touring productions.

places.name: Chayamachi spice curry counters
places.summary: Small counters serving Osaka-style spice curry, several curries on one plate with rice, at lunch.

places.name: Nakazakicho natural wine and craft bars
places.summary: A few snug bars in old houses pouring natural wine and craft beer to a small crowd.

places.name: Nakazakicho back-street izakaya
places.summary: Neighbourhood izakaya and yakitori grills on the streets between the station and the tracks.

places.name: Tenjinbashisuji Shopping Street
places.summary: About 2.6 km of covered arcade, the longest in Japan: croquettes, tea shops, cheap clothes and everything else.

places.name: Osaka Tenmangu
places.summary: The shrine to Sugawara no Michizane, god of learning, where students pray before exams and the Tenjin Matsuri begins.

places.name: Tenma Tenjin Hanjotei
places.summary: A rakugo theater beside the shrine, with storytellers on stage every day.

places.name: Osaka Museum of Housing and Living
places.summary: A full-size Edo-period Osaka street indoors, with houses to walk into and kimono to try on.

places.name: Tenma izakaya alleys
places.summary: Dozens of cheap, crowded izakaya, standing bars and seafood counters around JR Tenma station, spilling into the street.

places.name: Harukoma
places.summary: A cheap, popular sushi counter on Tenjinbashisuji with a queue at most hours.

places.name: Nakamuraya
places.summary: Takeaway croquette shop on the arcade, famous for hot, cheap potato korokke.

places.name: Tenma Market
places.summary: Old covered fresh market of fish, vegetables and pickles off the arcade, with cheap eateries round about.

places.name: Ogimachi Pool
places.summary: Municipal indoor pool and gym in Ogimachi Park, cheap per visit.

places.name: Japan Mint cherry blossom passage
places.summary: For one week in April the Mint opens its riverside lane of late-blooming cherry varieties to the public.

places.name: Tenjinbashisuji kissaten
places.summary: Old coffee shops along the arcade with morning sets, mix juice and regulars reading the paper.

places.name: Fukushima izakaya streets
places.summary: Back streets of small izakaya, yakitori grills and wine bars between JR Fukushima and the Hanshin line.

places.name: Hanakujira
places.summary: Oden shop with a famous queue for its dashi-soaked daikon, tofu and beef tendon.

places.name: Fukushima standing bars under the tracks
places.summary: Tiny tachinomi counters beneath the JR viaduct where office workers stop for a highball and skewers.

places.name: Osaka Municipal Central Wholesale Market
places.summary: The city's main fish and produce market at Noda, busiest before dawn; its restaurant row is open to the public.

places.name: Endo Sushi
places.summary: Early-morning sushi counter by the central market, serving plates of five pieces from the day's catch.

places.name: Nakanoshima Park
places.summary: Riverside lawns and a rose garden at the eastern end of the island, Osaka's first public park.

places.name: Osaka City Central Public Hall
places.summary: Red-brick and granite hall from 1918, paid for by a stockbroker's gift, still used for concerts and lectures.

places.name: Osaka Prefectural Nakanoshima Library
places.summary: The domed 1904 library beside City Hall, with business and Osaka history collections.

places.name: Nakanoshima Museum of Art, Osaka
places.summary: A black box of a museum opened in 2022, with modern art, design and big touring shows.

places.name: Festival Hall
places.summary: Concert hall with famous acoustics, rebuilt in 2013 inside a skyscraper, for orchestras, pop shows and kabuki.

places.name: Takamura Wine & Coffee Roasters
places.summary: A warehouse south of Higobashi that roasts its own coffee and sells wine, with long tables to linger at.

places.name: Festival City restaurant floors
places.summary: Restaurants and cafes in the twin Festival towers, from set lunches to river-view dinners.

places.name: Nakanoshima riverside bars
places.summary: A handful of bars and bistros looking onto the Dojima and Tosabori rivers, with terraces in fine weather.

places.name: Higobashi bistros and izakaya
places.summary: Small French bistros, wine bars and izakaya around Higobashi where office workers have dinner.

places.name: Nakanoshima Park cafes
places.summary: Cafes and kiosks by the rose garden and the riverside lawns.

places.name: Kitahama Retro
places.summary: An English-style tea room in a tiny 1912 brick building facing the river, known for afternoon tea and scones.

places.name: Brooklyn Roasting Company Kitahama
places.summary: Big, airy coffee shop facing the Tosabori river, with seats on the riverside terrace.

places.name: Kitahama Terrace
places.summary: Wooden decks along the Tosabori river behind cafes and restaurants, open from spring to autumn.

places.name: Tekijuku
places.summary: The Edo-period house of Ogata Koan's school of Dutch medicine, where Fukuzawa Yukichi studied; an ancestor of Osaka University.

places.name: Kitahama and Doshomachi lunch counters
places.summary: Spice curry, soba and teishoku counters with office-worker queues from noon to one.

places.name: Kitahama sake and wine bars
places.summary: Quiet bars in old office buildings serving regional sake and wine to the after-work crowd.

places.name: Utsubo Park
places.summary: A long green park on an old airfield, with a rose garden, zelkova trees and cafes on its edges.

places.name: Utsubo Tennis Center
places.summary: Public tennis courts in Utsubo Park, with a stadium court for tournaments.

places.name: Semba Center Building
places.summary: A kilometre-long building under the expressway full of textile and clothing wholesalers who sell to anyone.

places.name: Kyomachibori bistros
places.summary: Small restaurants and wine bars on the streets east of Utsubo Park, popular for dates.

places.name: Honmachi office lunch spots
places.summary: Udon, curry and teishoku set-meal shops in the side streets, all rushed at noon on weekdays.

places.name: Utsubo Park cafes
places.summary: Bakeries and coffee stands lining the park, with seats looking onto the trees.

places.name: Honmachi standing bars
places.summary: After-work tachinomi near the stations where suits stand elbow to elbow over beer and fried skewers.

places.name: Osaka Municipal Central Library
places.summary: The city's main library at Nishi-Nagahori, open late with big study floors.

places.name: Yoshino Sushi
places.summary: Old Semba shop serving Osaka-style hakozushi, pressed box sushi cut into neat squares, since the Edo period.

places.name: Shinsaibashi-suji Shopping Street
places.summary: The covered shopping arcade from Nagahori to Dotonbori, crowded with fashion chains, drugstores and visitors.

places.name: Daimaru Shinsaibashi
places.summary: Department store rebuilt in 2019 behind its old Vories facade, with a busy food hall in the basement.

places.name: Triangle Park (Mitsu Park)
places.summary: A small concrete square at the heart of Amerikamura where young people sit, eat takoyaki and watch the street.

places.name: Amerikamura vintage shops
places.summary: Used American clothes, sneakers, records and street fashion stacked into narrow buildings.

places.name: Kogaryu
places.summary: The Amerikamura takoyaki stand by Triangle Park, eaten standing or on the benches.

places.name: Usami-tei Matsubaya
places.summary: Old udon shop in Minami-Senba that claims to have invented kitsune udon, with sweet fried tofu on top.

places.name: LiLo Coffee Roasters
places.summary: Tiny specialty roaster in Nishi-Shinsaibashi with light-roast single origins and a few stools.

places.name: Amerikamura bars and clubs
places.summary: DJ bars, small clubs and late bars in the blocks around Triangle Park, busiest on Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Shinsaibashi Neon Shokudogai
places.summary: A basement food alley in Shinsaibashi PARCO, with neon-lit counters of gyoza, ramen and highballs.

places.name: Glico sign and Ebisubashi
places.summary: The running-man billboard over the canal, the city's favourite photo spot; the bridge below is where crowds gather to celebrate.

places.name: Tombori River Cruise
places.summary: Twenty-minute boat ride along the Dotonbori canal with a chatty guide.

places.name: Hozenji and Hozenji Yokocho
places.summary: A moss-covered Fudo statue people splash with water for luck, in a lantern-lit flagstone alley of small restaurants.

places.name: Kani Doraku Dotonbori Main Store
places.summary: Crab restaurant under the giant moving crab sign, serving crab courses in private rooms.

places.name: Takoyaki Dotonbori Kukuru
places.summary: Takoyaki stand with an octopus on the sign and big pieces of octopus inside, eaten at the counter or on the street.

places.name: Kinryu Ramen
places.summary: Pork-bone ramen under a dragon sign, open all night, with free kimchi and garlic on the counter.

places.name: Mizuno
places.summary: Family-run okonomiyaki shop since 1945, cooked on the griddle in front of you; expect a queue.

places.name: Arabiya Coffee
places.summary: Kissaten near Hozenji serving siphon coffee and toast since the early 1950s.

places.name: Kissa American
places.summary: Grand old kissaten from 1946 with chandeliers, thick hotcakes and waiters in bow ties.

places.name: Osaka Shochikuza
places.summary: A 1923 theater with an arched facade on the canal, staging kabuki, plays and musicals.

places.name: Namba Grand Kagetsu
places.summary: Yoshimoto's flagship comedy theater: manzai duos, then the slapstick Yoshimoto Shinkigeki troupe, several shows a day.

places.name: Namba Parks
places.summary: Mall stepping up in terraces of rooftop gardens behind Nankai Namba station.

places.name: Takashimaya Osaka
places.summary: The grand department store on top of Nankai Namba station, with a deep food hall and restaurant floors.

places.name: Sennichimae Doguyasuji
places.summary: Covered arcade of kitchenware shops: knives, takoyaki pans, plastic food samples and shop lanterns.

places.name: Takoyaki Wanaka Sennichimae Main Store
places.summary: Takoyaki shop by Namba Grand Kagetsu, crisp outside and molten inside, with a choice of sauces.

places.name: Jiyuken
places.summary: Western-style restaurant since 1910, known for curry already mixed into the rice and topped with a raw egg.

places.name: 551 Horai Main Store
places.summary: The pork bun shop on Ebisubashi-suji where the butaman are folded in the window; everyone queues.

places.name: Rikuro's Namba Main Store
places.summary: Bakery that rings a bell each time a jiggly baked cheesecake comes out of the oven.

places.name: Maru-Fuku Coffee Sennichimae Main Shop
places.summary: Dark, wood-panelled kissaten serving strong drip coffee and hotcakes since 1934.

places.name: Ura-Namba
places.summary: Back streets east of Namba packed with standing bars, oyster bars and tiny izakaya where strangers end up talking.

places.name: Edion Arena Osaka
places.summary: The prefectural gymnasium, home of the Spring Grand Sumo Tournament each March and of boxing and concerts the rest of the year.

places.name: Kuromon Market
places.summary: The covered "kitchen of Osaka": fish stalls, grilled scallops, fruit and wagyu skewers eaten on the spot.

places.name: National Bunraku Theatre
places.summary: The home of bunraku puppet theater, born in Osaka, with English earphone guides.

places.name: Den Den Town
places.summary: Electronics, anime, figure and card shops along Sakaisuji and Otaku Road.

places.name: Den Den Town game centers
places.summary: Floors of crane games, rhythm games and fighting-game cabinets.

places.name: Den Den Town maid cafes
places.summary: Themed cafes on Otaku Road where staff in costume serve omurice with drawings in ketchup.

places.name: Kuromon fugu and seafood restaurants
places.summary: Restaurants around the market serving pufferfish hot pot in winter and sashimi all year.

places.name: Sakaisuji ramen counters
places.summary: Ramen and gyoza counters feeding gamers and shop staff along Sakaisuji until late.

places.name: Nipponbashi game bars
places.summary: Small bars with consoles and anime on the screens, where regulars play and drink.

places.name: Tsutenkaku
places.summary: The 1956 steel tower over Shinsekai, with the lucky Billiken statue on the observation deck and an outdoor slide down the side.

places.name: Kushikatsu Daruma Shinsekai Main Store
places.summary: The 1929 kushikatsu counter whose angry-chef statue warns: no double-dipping in the sauce.

places.name: Yaekatsu
places.summary: Long-running kushikatsu counter in Janjan Yokocho with a constant queue and fast-moving cooks.

places.name: Tengu
places.summary: Kushikatsu and doteyaki beef-tendon stew at a crowded counter in Janjan Yokocho.

places.name: Janjan Yokocho
places.summary: A narrow covered alley of kushikatsu counters, standing bars and old men playing shogi in open-fronted parlors.

places.name: Shinsekai standing bars
places.summary: Cheap tachinomi where a beer, doteyaki and a chat with the regulars costs very little.

places.name: Shinsekai doteyaki and horumon stalls
places.summary: Stalls and counters simmering beef tendon in miso and grilling offal on the main street.

places.name: Spa World
places.summary: A huge onsen complex with themed European and Asian bath floors (alternating by gender month to month), a swimsuit pool zone and rest areas.

places.name: Tennoji Zoo
places.summary: A century-old city zoo between Shinsekai and Tennoji Park, with an African savanna zone.

places.name: Harukas 300
places.summary: Glass-walled observation floors at the top of the 300-metre Abeno Harukas, with views to Kobe and the bay at sunset.

places.name: Shitennoji
places.summary: One of Japan's oldest temples, founded by Prince Shotoku in 593, with a five-story pagoda and a monthly flea market.

places.name: Shitennoji flea market
places.summary: Stalls of antiques, old kimono, tools and snacks fill the temple grounds on the 21st and 22nd of each month.

places.name: Tennoji Park and Keitakuen Garden
places.summary: City park with a stroll garden around a pond, beside the zoo and the art museum.

places.name: Tennoshiba
places.summary: The lawn at the front of Tennoji Park ringed by cafes, a playground and a dog run.

places.name: Osaka City Museum of Fine Arts
places.summary: Asian art and big exhibitions in a 1936 building in Tennoji Park.

places.name: Abeno Harukas Kintetsu food hall
places.summary: Sprawling department store basement of bento, wagashi and deli counters under the tower.

places.name: Abeno Harukas restaurant floors
places.summary: Restaurant floors high in the tower, from tonkatsu to kaiseki, with views across the south of the city.

places.name: Ura-Tennoji
places.summary: Lanes behind Tennoji station full of small bars, yakitori and Spanish-style bars in old houses.

places.name: Tsuruhashi Market
places.summary: A dark, covered maze of kimchi stalls, Korean rice cakes, hanbok tailors, fish and dried goods beside the station.

places.name: Tsuruhashi yakiniku alleys
places.summary: Charcoal yakiniku shops crowded under the tracks, smoke rolling over the platforms.

places.name: Tsuruichi
places.summary: Long-established yakiniku house by Tsuruhashi station, with cuts grilled over charcoal and sauce made in the house.

places.name: Tsuruhashi Fugetsu Main Store
places.summary: Where the Fugetsu okonomiyaki chain started in 1950, cooked for you on the table griddle.

places.name: Ikuno Koreatown
places.summary: The Miyuki-dori shopping street of Korean groceries, cosmetics and K-pop goods, busy with young visitors at weekends.

places.name: Koreatown cafes and hotteok stands
places.summary: Korean cafes, cheese hotdog and hotteok stands along the shopping street.

places.name: Osaka Koreatown History Museum
places.summary: Small museum telling the century-long story of Korean residents in Ikuno.

places.name: Osaka Castle Main Tower
places.summary: The gold-trimmed 1931 concrete rebuild of Hideyoshi's keep, a museum of the castle's wars with a lookout on top.

places.name: Osaka Castle Park
places.summary: Huge park inside and around the moats, with a plum grove in February and thousands of cherry trees in April.

places.name: Nishinomaru Garden
places.summary: Lawn garden under the castle walls, a favourite hanami spot with evening cherry-blossom lighting.

places.name: Osaka Castle Park running loop
places.summary: The moat-side loops where half the city's runners train, with lockers and showers at the station.

places.name: Osaka-jo Hall
places.summary: Big arena in the castle park for pop concerts and sports.

places.name: Osaka Museum of History
places.summary: Museum that walks down through the centuries floor by floor, with views over the castle and the Naniwa palace site.

places.name: JO-TERRACE OSAKA
places.summary: Restaurants and cafes by Osakajokoen station, handy after a run or a concert.

places.name: Miraiza Osaka-jo
places.summary: Restaurants and a rooftop bar in a castle-style 1931 military headquarters inside the park.

places.name: Morinomiya izakaya
places.summary: Neighbourhood izakaya and yakitori around Morinomiya station, full of locals after work.

places.name: Osaka Castle hanami stalls
places.summary: Yatai selling takoyaki, yakisoba and beer along the paths at cherry blossom time.

places.name: Tanimachi lunch counters and kissaten
places.summary: Curry, udon and coffee shops along Tanimachi-suji feeding prefectural office workers.

places.name: Tachinomi Toyo
places.summary: Famous standing bar where the owner sears tuna with a blowtorch in front of the crowd.

places.name: Kyobashi standing bars
places.summary: Morning-to-night tachinomi around the station, some serving a beer at breakfast time.

places.name: Kyobashi Grand Chateau
places.summary: A 1970s leisure building of karaoke, bars and restaurants, famous for its old TV jingle.

places.name: Kyobashi arcade eateries
places.summary: Udon, gyoza, kushikatsu and teishoku shops along the arcade.

places.name: Kyobashi kissaten
places.summary: Old coffee shops with morning sets of toast, boiled egg and coffee for regulars reading the sports paper.

places.name: Kema Sakuranomiya Park
places.summary: Kilometres of cherry trees along the Okawa river, crowded with hanami parties in April and joggers all year.

places.name: Negiyaki Yamamoto Main Store
places.summary: Where negiyaki began in 1965: a thin savoury pancake buried in green onion, finished with lemon and soy.

places.name: Juso izakaya and bars
places.summary: Narrow streets west of Hankyu Juso station lined with cheap izakaya and standing bars.

places.name: Juso bakeries and kissaten
places.summary: Old kissaten and local bakeries in the arcades, with morning sets and sweet buns.

places.name: Juso late-night ramen and yakiniku
places.summary: Ramen counters and horumon grills that keep going after the bars close.

places.name: The Seventh Art Theater
places.summary: Independent mini-cinema showing documentaries and art films.

places.name: Yodogawa riverside park
places.summary: Wide grassy riverbanks along the Yodo with running and cycling paths and baseball fields.

places.name: Juso snack bars
places.summary: Tiny "sunakku" bars run by a mama-san, with a bottle kept for regulars and a karaoke machine in the corner.

places.name: Kaiyukan
places.summary: One of the world's largest aquariums, spiralling down around a giant central tank with a whale shark.

places.name: Naniwa Kuishinbo Yokocho
places.summary: A retro 1960s Osaka street inside Tempozan Marketplace with takoyaki, okonomiyaki and curry shops.

places.name: Universal Studios Japan
places.summary: The theme park at Sakurajima, with Super Nintendo World, the Wizarding World of Harry Potter and seasonal events.

places.name: Universal CityWalk Osaka
places.summary: Restaurants, takoyaki stands and shops outside the theme park gates.

places.name: Kyocera Dome Osaka
places.summary: Domed ballpark of the Orix Buffaloes and a stadium-size concert venue.

places.name: Taisho Okinawan eateries
places.summary: Okinawan shokudo and bars of Taisho ward, serving goya champuru, Okinawa soba and awamori.

places.name: Bentencho izakaya
places.summary: Plain izakaya and standing bars under the Loop Line at Bentencho station.

places.name: Osaka Pool
places.summary: The big municipal swimming pool by Asashiobashi station, with a 50 m pool open to the public.

places.name: Osaka Municipal Central Gymnasium
places.summary: Domed sports center under a grassy hill, with a public training room and studio classes.

places.name: Hirao shopping street
places.summary: Taisho's arcade with Okinawan groceries, sata andagi doughnuts and shops for the ward's Okinawan community.

places.name: Sumiyoshi Taisha
places.summary: Head of Japan's Sumiyoshi shrines, with its own ancient architecture and a steep red arched bridge over the pond.

places.name: Nagai Park
places.summary: Large park with a botanical garden, a natural history museum and two stadiums.

places.name: Nagai Park jogging course
places.summary: Measured running loop around the stadiums, busy with club runners.

places.name: Yodoko Sakura Stadium
places.summary: Football stadium in Nagai Park, home of Cerezo Osaka.

places.name: Sumiyoshi Taisha mochi and tea shops
places.summary: Old sweet shops by the shrine gates selling mochi and green tea to worshippers.

places.name: Sumiyoshi local shopping streets
places.summary: Small arcades of greengrocers, tofu makers and croquette counters near the tram stops.

places.name: Hankai tram-stop izakaya
places.summary: Family-run izakaya by the streetcar stops, with oden and highballs.

places.name: Sumiyoshi neighbourhood okonomiyaki
places.summary: Small okonomiyaki shops where the owner cooks on a griddle that fills the room.

places.name: Tezukayama bakeries and cafes
places.summary: Bakeries and quiet cafes in the leafy hill streets above the shrine.

places.name: Supermarket Tamade
places.summary: The neon-lit, all-hours discount supermarket chain born in Nishinari, known for very cheap bento.

places.name: Cocoroom
places.summary: Guesthouse, garden and cafe in Kamagasaki that runs poetry, art and study sessions with local residents.

places.name: Shin-Imamiya standing bars
places.summary: Some of the cheapest drinks in Japan, poured at counters near the station for regulars and backpackers.

places.name: Nishinari shokudo and horumon counters
places.summary: Cheap canteens serving set meals, doteyaki and grilled offal from early morning.

places.name: Tengachaya shopping street
places.summary: Old covered arcade of greengrocers, fishmongers and cheap clothes by the Nankai station.

places.name: Expo '70 Commemorative Park
places.summary: The grounds of the 1970 World Expo turned into a huge park of lawns, forests, a Japanese garden and seasonal flower fields.

places.name: Tower of the Sun
places.summary: Taro Okamoto's three-faced tower from Expo '70, which can be visited inside by reservation.

places.name: National Museum of Ethnology (Minpaku)
places.summary: One of the world's largest ethnology museums, with everyday objects from every continent.

places.name: EXPOCITY
places.summary: Mall beside Expo park with the Nifrel living museum, the Osaka Wheel and a food court.

places.name: EXPOCITY restaurants and food court
places.summary: Ramen, okonomiyaki, burgers and family restaurants under one roof.

places.name: Panasonic Stadium Suita
places.summary: Football stadium of Gamba Osaka, steep and loud, beside Expo park.

places.name: Esaka izakaya streets
places.summary: Bars and izakaya around Esaka station on the Midosuji line, popular with students and young workers.

places.name: Kandaimae student eateries
places.summary: Cheap ramen, curry and set-meal shops on the slope up to Kansai University.

places.name: Suita station cafes
places.summary: Chain and local coffee shops by the stations where students study over a single drink.

places.name: Esaka ramen and gyoza counters
places.summary: Ramen, gyoza and teishoku shops around Esaka station, open late.

places.name: Minoo Park and Minoo Falls
places.summary: A three-kilometre path up a wooded gorge to a 33-metre waterfall, at its best in autumn colours.

places.name: Minoo momiji tempura stands
places.summary: Shops on the path to the falls frying maple leaves in sweet batter, a snack found almost only here.

places.name: Katsuoji
places.summary: Mountain temple of winning luck, covered in small red daruma dolls left by visitors.

places.name: Minoh Beer
places.summary: Award-winning family craft brewery from Minoh, poured at its own taproom near the station.

places.name: Hattori Ryokuchi Park
places.summary: Big park with ponds, a riding ground and an open-air museum of old farmhouses.

places.name: Ishibashi Handai-mae eateries
places.summary: Cheap student restaurants and izakaya in the arcade below Osaka University's Toyonaka campus.

places.name: Toyonaka bakeries and cafes
places.summary: Neighbourhood bakeries and coffee shops by the Hankyu stations, busy with parents after school drop-off.

places.name: Minoh and Senri-Chuo izakaya
places.summary: Quiet suburban izakaya near the stations for a drink on the way home.

places.name: Daisen Kofun (Emperor Nintoku's tomb)
places.summary: The largest of the keyhole-shaped Mozu tombs, a UNESCO World Heritage site ringed by moats; walk the path round it.

places.name: Sakai City Museum
places.summary: Museum of Sakai's tombs, merchants and crafts in Daisen Park.

places.name: Sakai Plaza of Rikyu and Akiko
places.summary: Museum of tea master Sen no Rikyu and poet Yosano Akiko, both from Sakai, with tea served in its tea rooms.

places.name: Sakai Traditional Crafts Museum
places.summary: Knife smiths' showroom and shop where chefs buy Sakai kitchen knives.

places.name: Kanbukuro
places.summary: Sweet shop founded centuries ago, serving kurumi mochi in green bean paste, often over shaved ice in summer.

places.name: Sakai-Higashi izakaya
places.summary: Izakaya and standing bars around Sakai-Higashi station.

places.name: Sakai old-town eateries
places.summary: Soba, udon and okonomiyaki shops in the old town along the Hankai tram line.

places.name: Sakai kissaten
places.summary: Neighbourhood coffee shops with morning sets and newspapers.

places.name: Sakai harbour seafood shokudo
places.summary: Plain seafood canteens near the harbour serving rice bowls of the morning's fish.

employers.name: Panasonic
employers.summary: Electronics maker founded in Osaka by Konosuke Matsushita in 1918, headquartered in Kadoma, a short Keihan ride east of Kyobashi.

employers.name: Sharp
employers.summary: Electronics company founded in Osaka in 1912, with its head office on the Sakai waterfront.

employers.name: Daikin Industries
employers.summary: Air-conditioning maker with its head office in Umeda.

employers.name: Sakura Internet
employers.summary: Cloud and data-center company with its head office in Grand Front Osaka.

employers.name: Kansai Electric Power
employers.summary: Kanden, the utility that powers the Kansai region, run from its tower on the west of Nakanoshima.

employers.name: Takeda Pharmaceutical
employers.summary: Drug maker founded in Doshomachi, Osaka's old medicine merchants' street, in 1781; it keeps its Osaka head office there.

employers.name: Shionogi
employers.summary: Pharmaceutical company founded in Doshomachi in 1878, headquartered there still, with research labs in Toyonaka.

employers.name: Suntory
employers.summary: Whisky, beer and soft-drink company founded in Osaka in 1899, with its Osaka head office at Dojimahama by the river.

employers.name: Nissin Foods
employers.summary: The instant noodle company Momofuku Ando founded, with its Osaka head office in Yodogawa ward north of the river.

employers.name: Kintetsu Group
employers.summary: Japan's largest private railway group, headquartered in Uehommachi, which also runs Abeno Harukas, department stores and hotels.

employers.name: Hankyu Hanshin group
employers.summary: The group behind the Hankyu and Hanshin railways, the Umeda department stores, the Takarazuka Revue and the Hanshin Tigers.

employers.name: Osaka City Office
employers.summary: City Hall on Nakanoshima and the ward offices, including the board of education that runs the city's public schools.

employers.name: Osaka University Hospital
employers.summary: Teaching hospital on the Suita campus.

employers.name: Osaka Metropolitan University Hospital
employers.summary: University hospital at Abeno, a short walk from Tennoji station.

employers.name: Osaka International Cancer Institute
employers.summary: Prefectural cancer hospital and research center by Osaka Castle.

employers.name: Kitano Hospital
employers.summary: General hospital in Ogimachi, Kita ward.

employers.name: Universal Studios Japan
employers.summary: The Sakurajima theme park, one of the city's biggest hirers of performers, cooks and crew.

employers.name: Yoshimoto Kogyo
employers.summary: The comedy company founded in Osaka in 1912, running Namba Grand Kagetsu and a training school for manzai duos.

employers.name: Asahi Broadcasting (ABC TV)
employers.summary: Osaka TV and radio broadcaster at Hotarumachi, Fukushima.

employers.name: Port of Osaka
employers.summary: Container terminals at Nanko and Yumeshima, ferry piers and warehouses run by the city and private operators.

employers.name: Resona Bank
employers.summary: Bank with its registered head office in Osaka's Chuo ward.

employers.name: Osaka Exchange
employers.summary: Japan's derivatives exchange, part of Japan Exchange Group, in the old Osaka Stock Exchange building at Kitahama.

employers.name: Imperial Hotel Osaka
employers.summary: Grand hotel on the Okawa river across from the Mint.

career_hubs.name: Kita business district
career_hubs.summary: Head offices, banks, law firms and broadcasters in the towers around Umeda and Nakanoshima.

career_hubs.name: Semba and Kitahama
career_hubs.summary: The old merchant quarter: trading houses, textile wholesalers and the pharmaceutical street of Doshomachi.

career_hubs.name: Minami
career_hubs.summary: Restaurants, department stores, theaters, hotels and shops from Shinsaibashi down to Tennoji.

career_hubs.name: Osaka Bay
career_hubs.summary: The port, warehouses, the aquarium and the theme park along the bay.

career_hubs.name: Northern campuses and research parks
career_hubs.summary: Universities, hospitals and corporate labs in the northern suburbs.

climate.summary: Humid subtropical: mild, dry winters; a rainy season in June and early July; long, hot, humid summers with typhoons possible from August to October; and clear, comfortable autumns.

months.note: Coldest month; dry and clear, rarely any snow.
Cold and dry; plum blossoms open at the castle late in the month.
Changeable; cherry blossoms usually open in the last week.
Cherry blossoms early in the month; mild and pleasant.
Warm and sunny through Golden Week.
Tsuyu rainy season sets in; damp and muggy.
Rainy season ends mid-month, then hot, sticky festival nights.
Hottest month; heat warnings, cicadas and the odd typhoon.
Crisp and dry; autumn leaves in the parks and at Minoo.
Cool and dry; illuminations along Midosuji and Nakanoshima.

annual_events.name: Toka Ebisu
annual_events.summary: From the 9th to the 11th of January, crowds at Imamiya Ebisu Shrine buy bamboo branches hung with lucky charms for business in the year ahead.

annual_events.name: Doya Doya at Shitennoji
annual_events.summary: On January 14 teams in loincloths wrestle for paper charms showered down in the temple hall.

annual_events.name: Osaka Marathon
annual_events.summary: Late-February marathon through the center, from the prefectural offices by the castle out and back across the city.

annual_events.name: Spring Grand Sumo Tournament
annual_events.summary: Fifteen days of top-division sumo at Edion Arena each March, with wrestlers seen around Namba.

annual_events.name: Cherry blossom season
annual_events.summary: Hanami picnics under the trees at Osaka Castle, Sakuranomiya and Expo park from late March into early April.

annual_events.name: Mint Bureau cherry blossom passage
annual_events.summary: One week in mid-April when the Japan Mint opens its riverside lane of late-blooming cherry trees.

annual_events.name: Aizen Matsuri
annual_events.summary: From June 30 to July 2 at Aizendo near Shitennoji, the first of Osaka's summer festivals, with yukata-clad women carried in palanquins.

annual_events.name: Tenjin Matsuri
annual_events.summary: On July 24 and 25, one of Japan's three great festivals: a land procession from Osaka Tenmangu, a hundred boats on the Okawa river and fireworks overhead.

annual_events.name: Sumiyoshi Matsuri
annual_events.summary: Summer purification festival at Sumiyoshi Taisha, ending on August 1 with a portable shrine carried to Sakai.

annual_events.name: Naniwa Yodogawa Fireworks
annual_events.summary: A summer night of fireworks over the Yodo river near Juso, watched from packed riverbanks.

annual_events.name: Summer Koshien high school baseball
annual_events.summary: The national high school baseball championship at Koshien Stadium in Nishinomiya, a short Hanshin ride away; the whole region watches on TV.

annual_events.name: Kishiwada Danjiri Matsuri
annual_events.summary: In Kishiwada, south of Sakai, teams haul heavy carved wooden floats through the streets at a run, taking corners at speed.

annual_events.name: Midosuji Autumn Party
annual_events.summary: A day when Midosuji boulevard closes to traffic for parades, marching bands and stalls under the ginkgo trees.

annual_events.name: OSAKA Hikari-Renaissance
annual_events.summary: Light shows projected on the Central Public Hall and illuminations along Nakanoshima through December.

annual_events.name: Midosuji Illumination
annual_events.summary: Kilometres of Midosuji's ginkgo trees strung with lights from November to the new year.

local_color.name: Takoyaki
local_color.summary: Batter balls with octopus inside, turned with picks in a dimpled pan, topped with sauce, mayonnaise, aonori and bonito flakes; many families own a takoyaki pan.

local_color.name: Okonomiyaki
local_color.summary: The savoury cabbage pancake cooked on a griddle, Osaka style with everything mixed into the batter, often eaten with rice as a set.

local_color.name: Kushikatsu
local_color.summary: Deep-fried skewers of meat, vegetables and cheese, dipped once in a shared tin of sauce; "no double-dipping" is the rule, and cabbage scoops more sauce.

local_color.name: Kitsune udon
local_color.summary: Udon in light kombu dashi topped with sweet fried tofu, an Osaka invention; locals insist the soup should be clear, not dark like Tokyo's.

local_color.name: 551 Horai butaman
local_color.summary: Big pork buns bought by the box at the station and carried home or to the office; the TV ad line goes "when there is 551, everyone smiles".

local_color.name: Negiyaki and ikayaki
local_color.summary: Negiyaki is a thin pancake buried in green onion; ikayaki is Osaka's squid-and-egg pancake folded in paper, eaten standing in the Hanshin basement.

local_color.name: Mix juice
local_color.summary: A kissaten classic: banana, peach, orange and milk blended smooth and served cold.

local_color.name: Highball
local_color.summary: Whisky and soda in a big mug, the default order in standing bars and izakaya alongside a beer.

local_color.name: "Maido"
local_color.summary: The all-purpose shopkeeper's greeting, "thanks as always", which the abacus-shaking merchant spirit of the city boils down to.

local_color.name: "Ookini"
local_color.summary: Osaka-ben for thank you, still heard from older shopkeepers and taxi drivers.

local_color.name: "Nande ya nen"
local_color.summary: The comedian's "what do you mean?!", the tsukkomi line everyone in Osaka uses to snap back at nonsense.

local_color.name: "Mokarimakka?" "Bochi bochi denna"
local_color.summary: The merchants' joke greeting, "making money?" answered with "so-so", said half in earnest.

local_color.name: "Honma" and "akan"
local_color.summary: Osaka-ben for "really" and "no good", used in every second sentence.

local_color.name: Kuidaore
local_color.summary: Osaka's motto of eating until you drop, or eating yourself into ruin: food is where the money goes. Its mascot, Kuidaore Taro, a drum-beating clown doll, stands outside a Dotonbori building.

local_color.name: Standing on the right
local_color.summary: On Osaka escalators people stand on the right and walk on the left, the opposite of Tokyo.

local_color.name: Boke and tsukkomi
local_color.summary: Conversations run like manzai: one person plays the fool and the other slaps back with the correction, and a story without a punchline is complained about.

local_color.name: "Nanbo?" and haggling
local_color.summary: Osakans ask "how much?" and push for "makete" (a discount), and like to tell you how cheaply they got something.

local_color.name: Osaka obachan and ame-chan
local_color.summary: The neighbourhood aunties, famous for loud prints, bicycles and handing candy ("ame-chan") to strangers on trains.

local_color.name: Mamachari
local_color.summary: Everyday city bicycles with baskets and child seats ridden on the pavements, often holding an umbrella, and parked by the hundred at every station.

local_color.name: Billiken
local_color.summary: The grinning god of things as they ought to be; people rub the soles of his feet in Tsutenkaku for luck.

local_color.name: Depachika and konbini
local_color.summary: Department store basements for gifts and evening bento discounts, and a Lawson, FamilyMart or 7-Eleven on every corner for everything else.

local_color.name: Hanshin Tigers
local_color.summary: The baseball team followed with near-religious devotion; fans sing "Rokko Oroshi" at Koshien, and after the 2023 Japan Series title some jumped off Ebisubashi into the canal.

local_color.name: Orix Buffaloes
local_color.summary: Osaka's other baseball team, playing at Kyocera Dome, Pacific League champions three years running from 2021.

local_color.name: Gamba Osaka
local_color.summary: J.League football club in blue and black, playing at Panasonic Stadium Suita.

local_color.name: Cerezo Osaka
local_color.summary: The city's pink-shirted J.League club, named for the cherry blossom, at Nagai Park.

local_color.name: Expo 2025 memories
local_color.summary: The 2025 World Expo ran on the reclaimed island of Yumeshima from April to October 2025; Myaku-Myaku, its red and blue mascot, still turns up on souvenirs, and the island is now being rebuilt for a planned integrated resort.

local_color.name: Ehomaki at Setsubun
local_color.summary: On Setsubun in early February people eat a whole uncut sushi roll in silence, facing the year's lucky direction, a custom spread from Osaka.

prices.per: udon, curry or a set meal
for one, with a couple of drinks
a day's take-home for an ordinary job
